approval: A person approves: read each requirement's state and evidence, answer the questions, then run the next steps as dry runs. Nothing here writes to Fabric.

example_queries.query:
-- R1: Revenue per customer and month
-- invoiced net value (billing documents); rules RQ-M1 (RQ1-1 (19 November 2026)); no row value here
SELECT SUM(h.[NETWR]) AS net_value, h.[MANDT] AS client, h.[KUNAG] AS customer, SUBSTRING(REPLACE(CAST(h.[FKDAT] AS VARCHAR(30)), '-', ''), 1, 6) AS month, h.[WAERK] AS currency
FROM [sap].[sap_vbrk] AS h
GROUP BY h.[MANDT], h.[KUNAG], SUBSTRING(REPLACE(CAST(h.[FKDAT] AS VARCHAR(30)), '-', ''), 1, 6), h.[WAERK]
example_queries.question: Revenue per customer and month

example_queries.query:
-- R2: Order value per material and month
-- net value of the sales orders; rules RQ-M2 (RQ1-1 (19 November 2026)); no row value here
SELECT SUM(i.[NETWR]) AS net_value, h.[MANDT] AS client, i.[MATNR] AS material, SUBSTRING(REPLACE(CAST(h.[ERDAT] AS VARCHAR(30)), '-', ''), 1, 6) AS month, h.[WAERK] AS currency
FROM [sap].[sap_vbap] AS i
JOIN [sap].[sap_vbak] AS h ON i.[MANDT] = h.[MANDT] AND i.[VBELN] = h.[VBELN]
GROUP BY h.[MANDT], i.[MATNR], SUBSTRING(REPLACE(CAST(h.[ERDAT] AS VARCHAR(30)), '-', ''), 1, 6), h.[WAERK]
example_queries.question: Order value per material and month

columns: VBRK.NETWR (net value of the billing document (header))
notes: Customer here is the sold-to party (VBRK.KUNAG); the payer (VBRK.KUNRG) can be another customer. Write 'payer' in the requirement to use the payer.

requirements.text: Order value per material and month
traps: VBAK.NETWR is the whole document's value and repeats on every VBAP row: summing it per material counts each document once per line. Sum VBAP.NETWR instead (done in the query below). In the data, VBAP has 1.67 rows per VBAK row on average and up to 3.
1 VBAP row(s) point at no VBAK row (1 of 6 rows (16.7%) point at nothing): the join leaves them out. In silver they go to quarantine with the reason; decide in the review whether that is right.

missing.or: LIKP.LFDAT (planned delivery date) says when it was due, not when it left
missing.why: when the goods actually left; LIKP.ERDAT is when the delivery was created

requirements.say: A late delivery compares the date the customer asked for with the date the goods left.

missing.or: BSAD (cleared items) with BSEG.AUGDT, or ACDOCA with its clearing date; in S/4HANA the open items are in ACDOCA
missing.why: open customer items say which invoices are unpaid

requirements.say: Billing documents say what was invoiced, not what was paid: the payments are in accounting.
